name: Georgia
headline_status: Recreational marijuana is illegal; registered patients can buy medical cannabis products, and a 2026 law removed the 5% THC cap.
summary: Georgia began with a 2015 law letting registered patients possess low-THC oil, and the 2019 Hope Act created licensed production, with pharmacy and dispensary sales starting in summer 2023. In May 2026 Gov. Brian Kemp signed SB 220, which removes the 5% THC cap in favor of a 12,000 mg possession limit, allows vaporization for patients over 21 (smoking stays banned), and adds conditions such as lupus and inflammatory bowel disease. Recreational use remains illegal, and possessing an ounce or less is a misdemeanor that can bring up to a year in jail. A separate 2026 hemp law, SB 33, bans hemp products above 0.3% total THC.

medical_since.value: A 2015 law allowed registered patients to possess up to 20 fluid ounces of low-THC oil; the 2019 Hope Act (HB 324) authorized in-state production, and sales began in summer 2023.

medical_program.value: Patients with a qualifying condition and a physician's certification join the Department of Public Health's registry. Under SB 220 (signed May 12, 2026) the 5% THC cap is gone, patients may hold up to 12,000 mg of THC, and qualifying out-of-state patients are recognized.

medical_product_forms.value: Oils, tinctures, capsules, lozenges, patches and lotions are allowed; SB 220 adds vaporization for patients over 21 once rules are in place. Smoking, cannabis-infused foods and public use remain banned.

retail_sales.value: Medical-only. As of 2025, 63 independent pharmacies and 19 outlets run by vertically integrated licensees served about 33,300 active patients; six producers hold cultivation licenses.

regulator.value: Georgia Access to Medical Cannabis Commission licenses producers and dispensaries; the Department of Public Health runs the patient registry.

penalties.value: A first offense for possessing one ounce or less is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in jail. Some cities and counties have adopted local decriminalization ordinances.

hemp_thc.value: SB 33 (signed May 11, 2026) bans selling hemp products whose total THC or other intoxicating cannabinoids exceed 0.3%.

timeline.event: Gov. Nathan Deal signs HB 1 letting registered patients possess low-THC oil

faq.a: Recreational marijuana is illegal. Registered medical patients can buy and possess cannabis products from licensed pharmacies and dispensaries.

faq.q: Did Georgia remove the 5% THC limit?
faq.a: Yes. SB 220, signed May 12, 2026, replaces the 5% cap with a 12,000 mg total THC possession limit for registered patients.

faq.q: Can medical patients smoke or vape cannabis in Georgia?
faq.a: Smoking stays banned. SB 220 allows patients over 21 to vaporize approved products once state rules are in place.

faq.q: What is the penalty for weed possession in Georgia?
faq.a: Possessing an ounce or less is a misdemeanor that can bring up to a year in jail for a first offense, though some cities have local ordinances with lighter penalties.

faq.q: Is delta-8 or hemp THC legal in Georgia?
faq.a: SB 33, signed in May 2026, bans selling hemp products with more than 0.3% total THC or other intoxicating cannabinoids.
